body:
Correction to my last message, within the hour and on the smallest claim in it — but it was wrong in a way that would have sent you looking in the wrong place.

I wrote: "`aida history events --id BUG-1288` returned nothing for all three specs… The documented source of truth is currently unreachable through its own surface."

The command does not return nothing. It errors:

    $ aida history events --id BUG-1288
    error: unexpected argument '--id' found

`--id` does not exist. `aida history events --help` offers `--format` and `--help`, and that is the entire surface. The binary is 0.15.0 built today at 09:12 from sha 5aee18b91d, so it is not a stale-binary artifact, and there is no id filter on that subcommand in cli.rs.

I reported it as silence because I had run it with `2>/dev/null` and never saw the error. That is a smaller mistake than the two earlier ones but a more embarrassing kind: I suppressed the channel that was telling me the answer, then described the silence I had manufactured. "This surface returns nothing" and "this flag does not exist" send a reader to completely different places.

Filed as BUG-1474. CLAUDE.md's paragraph on spec-state history describes `aida history events [--id <spec-id|uuid>]` in some detail — what it accepts, that the UUID resolves to a spec_id — and cites BUG-588. BUG-588 is Completed and is about `aida edit` not writing `history:` array rows; it is not about this flag. So the citation does not support the claim attached to it, and the documented surface appears never to have been built, or to have been removed.

The practical consequence stands and is the reason I am not just quietly fixing the doc: the paragraph exists to tell a reader where to look for a spec's state history, and explicitly tells reviewers doing status-flow analysis to use it. That is exactly what I needed today to settle our disagreement, and the documented path fails. The four-line git-log recipe that did work is in the spec.

One acceptance criterion I would flag for your read: I suggested a check that documented `aida <cmd> --flag` invocations in CLAUDE.md actually parse. That is cheap and would have caught this, but it is also the kind of guard that becomes instance seven of SPIKE-85 if it is not careful about its own scope — a doc-checker that does not check the doc that describes it. Your call whether it belongs in this spec or is deliberately left out.
